A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FedRTS. Their text, figures, tables, equations and scientific appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated content and accounting for the removed submission checklist.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix E report original federated-learning experiments, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, robustness tests and training-cost results.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix F retain original empirical evaluations of FedRTS on computer-vision datasets and TinyStories, with updated comparisons in Figure 3.

M1.justification: TSAdj and FedRTS retain the same posterior updates, outcome fusion, top-K selection and two-loop training procedure. Algorithms 1–3 match; the new implementation and complexity explanations do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Coverage remains CIFAR-10, CINIC-10, TinyImageNet, SVHN and TinyStories, with the same classification and language-modeling tasks and client-heterogeneity and participation scenarios.

E2.justification: Figure 3 adds a FedTiny curve to the ResNet18/TinyImageNet comparison. This series was absent in v2 despite FedTiny appearing in the shared legend and other panels. Other main-text and appendix comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Training budgets, client counts, optimizers, batch sizes, density settings, preprocessing and evaluation metrics match. Figure 3 revises plotted communication costs without changing the stated cost-calculation protocol.

E4.justification: Figure 6 and v2 Appendix E/v3 Appendix F retain the same ablations, hyperparameter sweeps, convergence analyses, heterogeneity tests and FedCUCB/quantization studies. No new empirical robustness or diagnostic analysis is introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five repetitions, mean results and standard-error reporting in Section 4. Removing the checklist also removes v2's explicit statement that repetitions used different random seeds; v3 does not repeat that clarification elsewhere.

E6.justification: Figure 3 adds FedTiny results for ResNet18/TinyImageNet. For ShuffleNetV2/TinyImageNet, FedMef and FedSGC move to higher communication-cost ratios while retaining their accuracies. The leftmost PruneFL point's uncertainty band narrows in the ResNet18/TinyImageNet panel. Tables 1–4 and the other figures retain their results.

T1.justification: New Section 3.3 supplies an operation-wise server-complexity argument, claiming O(|C_t||W|) cost and comparing it with baseline complexities. The existing regret assumptions, Theorem 3.4 and Appendix C proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same CMAB-based novelty claim, robustness and efficiency contributions, and CV/NLP performance claims, including the stated 5.1% accuracy improvement and 33.3% communication reduction.

C2.justification: Appendix D adds warnings about gradient-index information leakage and bias toward data-rich clients. Broader Impact extends the existing fairness discussion with continual-learning recommendations. Section 3.3 newly argues that server overhead is insignificant.

D1.justification: Section 3.3 newly names Quicksort as the server's outcome-computation routine. This is additional implementation disclosure, not evidence of an implementation change. Hardware, training hyperparameters, preprocessing and the main code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds contextual references concerning federated learning, quantization, IoT, edge perception, medical applications and continual learning. Appendix A's substantive positioning against existing pruning and CMAB approaches remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes are localized: an overhead subsection, expanded notation explanations, revised limitations and Broader Impact, updated author details and funding acknowledgments. Broader Impact moves earlier in the appendices, and the submission checklist is removed; the main narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 gains a comparison series. Appendix Figures 9–14 are regrouped onto one page, and other floats shift with text reflow. The fifteen-figure, four-table inventory and overall visual style are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 fills a missing Figure 3 comparison and adds useful privacy qualifications. However, its new overhead argument assigns linear complexity to a stated Quicksort routine and infers insignificant overhead from matching asymptotic orders without measurements. The explicit different-seeds disclosure also disappears. These benefits and weaknesses leave the net quality effect unclear, while the core method and existing proofs remain unchanged.
